note: Rejudged Section 4.1: The receiver MUST process the packets from the different SAs without prejudice. The next sentence expressly binds both transport and tunnel mode. TestRFC4301ParallelSAsWithOneSelectorAreEachReceived drives two genuine tunnel Child SAs with one shared selector, sends first/second/first and requires all deliveries. The updated negative sends the unchanged outside-source packet on each SA and requires no delivery and exactly one receiving-state mismatch per SA, with both SPD counters unchanged; it therefore preserves that tunnel proof after state-selector binding. The SAD boundary pair separately keeps distinct SPIs and refuses unbuildable states. These tests establish useful tunnel-mode behavior but never exercise two transport-mode SAs: parallelChildPair always leaves transport disabled. The earlier whole-requirement enforced verdict therefore claims more than the tagged fixtures establish for the two modes the RFC explicitly names. Tests and tags are retained; a transport counterpart is owed.
